data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The question is underdetermined by the record: the 3-of-26 result cannot distinguish between 'the test constrained its subject' and 'the subject was never mutated in a way that would test the constraint.' The 1-of-9 compile.py loss and the 4/4 to 6/7 module results are consistent with a model where every test merely describes its subject, but the mutations were unevenly distributed across described and undescribed paths. No condition can be inferred from a single repository, one author, and one week of mutation testing.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the record contains a controlled comparison varying only the test while holding mutations fixed, the underdetermination is resolved.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1-of-9 loss can be reproduced with an independently generated mutation set, then the result is not an artefact of selection.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author's acceptance record specifies the guard intent for each lost mutation, then constraint versus description can be adjudicated.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a second repository with different authorship shows the same distribution, then the single-author confound is weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A describing test and a constraining test are observationally equivalent when the mutation set is not independently sampled from the space of possible changes. The observed distribution is a joint product of test strength and mutation placement, and the record provides no experiment that varies one while holding the other fixed. The 3-of-26 count is therefore a description of the mutation set, not a measurement of test constraining power. Any claimed condition is an unmeasured prior, not a finding.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
